_about: Levels of the landing window game (docs/design/mini-oyun.md, UC-17). The goals are game targets, not mission requirements. They were checked against the product's own computation: see 'calibration' on each level. Texts hold no numbers except the calibration notes, which quote the server's answers.

levels.title: Apollo 11, December 2026
levels.intro: A site near the equator, where Apollo 11 landed. Pick a landing date that gives your two-week mission enough daylight and short nights.
levels.calibration: Live server, 14 November 2026 (UTC), 2 m mast (flat horizon at this site): all three goals hold for landings on 12 to 18 December; Earth is in view the whole time on every date.

levels.title: Mons Mouton, December 2026
levels.intro: Near the south pole Earth can sink below the horizon for days. Land on the wrong date and you lose contact with home.

intro_source.label: JPL Horizons, Earthset and Earthrise at the Mons Mouton test site, December 2026

levels.calibration: Live server, 14 November 2026 (UTC), 2 m mast (terrain horizon): the Earth goal fails for landings on 1 to 5 December (Earth in view 63 to 68 percent of the mission) and holds from 6 December; all three goals hold for 12 to 19 December.

levels.title: Chang'e 4, December 2026
levels.intro: This site is on the far side of the Moon. Can you find a date when your lander can talk to Earth?
levels.calibration: Live server, 14 November 2026 (UTC), 2 m mast (flat horizon at this site): Earth is in view zero percent of the time on every date; the Sun goals hold for landings on 1 to 4 and 29 to 30 December.

never_earth.text: Earth never rose above the horizon during your mission. This site is on the far side: when it was checked for a whole year, Earth stayed below the horizon all the time. A lander here needs a relay satellite to talk to Earth.
